title: Quantized runloop slimdown and sticky cache protocol
creator: Priya Patel
description: Background: The continuous batching runloop has accumulated multiple ad-hoc scheduling paths and an oversized lease-based cache contract that increases tail latency under multi-tenant loads. This ticket aims to reduce runtime complexity by refactoring the runloop into a quantized scheduler (coarse time quanta for admission + lightweight worklets) and introduce a "sticky cache" protocol: a cheaper cache-lease shim that keeps hot KV entries pinned on best-effort heuristics rather than heavy-weight epoch checkpoints. Scope: refactor runloop to use a single timer wheel quantization, extract admission logic into a small state machine, replace heavyweight KV lease checkpoints with a sticky cache guard, and add health and telemetry hooks for rollout. Out of scope: full model swap orchestration, IPC layer changes, and customer-facing API changes. Goal: reduce 99th percentile latency spikes caused by scheduling jitter and KV lease contention, and simplify code paths to make later dependency upgrades (libaio, custom allocator) safer.
acceptance_criteria: Runloop refactor merged and feature-flag controlled (flag: runtime.quantized_runloop) with fallback to current path
End-to-end e2e perf test shows max 99p latency improvement >= 20% for steady-state batching workloads (internal benchmark: impute-batch-100)
KV cache memory overhead reduced by at least 15% in integration cluster under mixed traffic
No increase in token-level throughput regression > 2% on canary fleet
Observability: per-tenant queue depth, admission rejects, cache-guard-hits/misses counters are available in Console dashboard and traced in OpenTelemetry
technical_notes: Quantized scheduler: 8ms quanta chosen based on token generation distributions (see perf/quantization-2026-02-10.csv) - trade-off: coarser quanta reduces scheduling jitter but may increase average enqueue delay for ultra-low-latency singleton requests
Admission state machine: separate 'admit/park/evict' states; admission decisions now deterministic given queue depth and tenant credit bucket - simplifies backpressure surface
Sticky cache protocol: implement per-shard LRU with sticky bit; sticky entries bypass lease renewal until eviction candidate; lease checkpoint logic reduced to background compaction once per 30s
Memory accounting: switch cache accounting to sampled slab metrics to avoid hot counters; this avoids cache lock ping-pong seen in stress test #42
Compatibility: sticky protocol is backward compatible with existing checkpointing; during rollout sticky entries will be translated to epoch tags for observers
Observability hooks: emit compacted metrics (cache_guard_hits, cache_guard_evictions, runloop_quantum_ms) and trace spans for admission decisions

Trade-offs: sticky cache reduces lease churn but accepts a slightly higher risk of stale KV values for ephemeral sessions. Mitigation: short sticky lifetime for non-idempotent workloads and quick invalidation signal path built into the API gateway
steps: 1) Prototype quantized timer wheel in a feature branch (ENG-118433-quant-wheel)
2) Extract admission logic into runloop/admission module with unit tests
3) Implement sticky cache shim behind feature flag and internal API layer
4) Add telemetry instrumentation and dashboard panels (Console ticket: PM-5982)
5) Canary rollout to internal staging, run perf suite (impute-batch-100, chat-sustained-50) and load tests
6) Iterate on tuning (quantum size, sticky TTL) based on telemetry, then Gated rollout to production with kill-switch

impact: Expected to reduce tail latency spikes and simplify future dependency upgrades. Short-term risk: transient stale KV in degenerate corner cases mitigated by conservative TTL and invalidation signals.
